A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RL-AWB framework, SGP-LRD estimator, and LEVI dataset. Their complete main texts and appendices, including equations, tables, and figures, support reliable comparison despite substantial reformatting.

before.justification: v1 reports original illumination-estimation experiments on NCC, LEVI, and Gehler-Shi, alongside curriculum, RL-algorithm, and network-architecture ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains original benchmark results and reports expanded baseline comparisons, filtering-component ablations, inference timing, and illustrated failure cases.

M1.justification: Equation 7 changes the specified reward by removing epsilon = 0.001 from its denominator. The SGP-LRD pipeline, SAC architecture, parameter-update actions, and two-stage curriculum remain intact. The revised history description specifies parameter values, which were already described in v1 Appendix F, so that wording does not establish an input change.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate NCC, the same 700-image, two-camera LEVI dataset, and Gehler-Shi, covering nighttime estimation, cross-dataset transfer, and daytime generalization. Additional qualitative and failure examples do not establish a distinct dataset, population, or testing scenario.

E2.justification: FFCC, FC4, and GCC become evaluated comparators in the nighttime in-dataset and cross-dataset experiments; v1 cited these works but did not report these comparisons. Conversely, v1 Table 6's statistical-method reproduction-error comparisons are absent from v2. Mean Shift is renamed MSGP with the same reference and scores, rather than replaced.

E3.justification: v1 describes five-image training for C4, C5(5), and PCC, with a separate fully trained C5 comparison. v2 describes full-data, three-fold protocols for all learning-based baselines while retaining five-image RL-AWB training. Section 5.1 also changes the reported discount factor from 0.99 to 0.1 and training budget from 150,000 to 15,000 timesteps. These are reported setting revisions, not proof of rerunning experiments. Gehler-Shi evaluation additionally reports tri-mean.

E4.justification: v2 adds a focused ablation of noise and color filtering in Table 5, two over-correction trajectories in Figure 7, and additional qualitative comparisons in Figure 9. These extend component and failure analysis. Existing curriculum-size, network-architecture, and SAC-versus-PPO ablations remain; the latter moves from v1 Table 5 to v2 Appendix Table 10.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-seed variability, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Both summarize errors across test images using statistics such as means, medians, and best/worst quartiles. The expanded cross-validation protocols do not introduce uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Comparator scores and rankings change substantially under revised training protocols: NCC C4 median error is 6.24 degrees in v1 Table 1's five-image comparison and 1.66 in v2 Table 6's full-data comparison, while RL-AWB remains at 1.98. These are not comparable-setting performance gains. v2 also adds baseline rows, Gehler-Shi tri-means, filtering-ablation results, failure trajectories, and timing results, while removing statistical-method reproduction-error entries. Most retained RL-AWB benchmark values are unchanged.

T1.justification: The explicit uniform-illumination qualification preceding Equation 1 is omitted in v2, although the same derivation remains. Equation 7 also changes its mathematical definition by removing the positive denominator stabilizer. The remaining estimator and SAC equations and reproduction-error definition are retained, with no new theorem or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same central claims: a nighttime statistical estimator, the first reinforcement-learning approach to color constancy, adaptive tuning with five training images, and the first multi-camera nighttime dataset with strong cross-sensor generalization.

C2.justification: v2 reframes in-dataset performance as data-efficient competitiveness against fully trained baselines. It newly identifies near-achromatic-pixel dependence and abrupt illumination boundaries as limitations, and specifies low initial error as an over-correction condition; over-correction itself was already acknowledged in v1 Appendix G. New passages explain GCC failures through noise and domain shift and SAC's advantage through replay and off-policy learning.

D1.justification: v2 Appendix B newly specifies LoG sigma and approximate kernel size, dataset-specific variance/color thresholds, a confidence threshold, and selection by validation-set grid search. Section 5.1 adds average inference iterations, runtime, and RTX 3090 measurement hardware, alongside revised training settings. Existing software information, CPU/GPU implementation descriptions, and project-page access remain.

R1.justification: Section 2 substantially expands the literature context, with references increasing from 73 to 125. Added discussions cover gamut mapping, Bayesian estimation, GAN and meta-learning approaches, differentiable ISP, algorithm unrolling, and broader curriculum-learning foundations. This expands research positioning beyond citation renumbering or bibliographic corrections.

P1.justification: Most introductory, methodological, and concluding prose and the main section order remain. v2 expands related-work paragraphs, revises experimental and appendix summaries, adds explicit limitations and front-matter details, and inserts an additional visual-comparison appendix section. These are localized narrative changes rather than a wholesale rewrite.

P2.justification: The document changes from two-column to single-column formatting throughout. v1 Figures 4 and 5 merge into v2 Figure 4; the cross-dataset comparison figure changes comparator columns; new failure and supplementary comparison figures are added. Tables are reorganized between main text and appendices, the in-dataset comparison is split, and Gehler-Shi gains a tri-mean column.

improvement.justification: v2 provides broader comparisons against fully trained baselines, direct filtering ablations, concrete failure examples, and previously missing implementation parameters, improving evaluation and transparency. The gains are tempered by removing statistical-method reproduction results and introducing inaccurate summaries: Appendix E.2 calls C5 best on NCC, although Table 7 gives C4 lower median and mean reproduction errors. Overall, the added evidence and disclosure provide a useful but limited net improvement.
